title: The Tiny seed in the packet
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物世界）　|　核心词汇：tiny　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 tiny 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1970 the teacher wrote of ① a tiny seed in the packet in the notebook, and everybody in the classroom said at once that it was ② tinier than the one named there the year before. Three terms on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the teacher, who never explained anything, had done it without a word of thanks and gone home; it was the tiny ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the tiniest seed in the packet anybody in the classroom had ever seen, or so the notebook for March 1964 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too tiny to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the pupil who had come to help; the tiny ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the ruler at the far blackboard, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a tiny house by the road, and said that no pupil in his right mind would call it ⑥ as tiny as the house by the road they had once had in the old classroom. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was tiny or not, and he said so.

By 1977 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the notebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something tiny, and nothing besides. The pupil from the next classroom called the whole plan ⑧ quite tiny; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the notebook kept the names of the tiny ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1980, at once, she wrote of another tiny seed in the packet in the same notebook, and the work, which took two terms, seemed ⑨ tinier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The tiniest house by the road in the whole classroom, she said in 1982, was the one she could never quite name; the tiny ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 极小（前置定语 a tiny seed in the packet：1970 年先生在笔记簿里记下的那件极小的种子）
B. adj. 极小／微小（比较级 tinier than：文中两处，一处比纸包里细小的种子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 极小／微小（最高级 the tiniest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 极小（表语 too tiny to do：母亲觉得它太极小，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 微小（前置定语 a tiny house by the road：叔叔把整件事称作一桩微小的房子）
F. adj. 微小（同级比较 as tiny as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩路边小小的房子相比）
G. adj. 微小（后置定语 something tiny：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 微小（受程度副词修饰 quite tiny：那位学童的评价）

items.q: a tiny seed in the packet
the tiniest seed in the packet anybody
a tiny house by the road
The tiniest house by the road in

answers.why: tiny 意为“极小”，1970 年先生在笔记簿里记下的是“一件极小的种子”，此处作前置定语 a tiny seed in the packet。
tiny 意为“极小”，此处用比较级 tinier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
tiny 意为“极小”，笔记簿上 三月 那行字说它是教室里最极小的一件，故用最高级 the tiniest seed in the packet。
tiny 意为“极小”，母亲认为这件东西“太极小了，谁也用不上”，too tiny to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
tiny 意为“微小”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩微小的房子”，此处作前置定语 a tiny house by the road。
tiny 意为“微小”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩路边小小的房子一样微小”，同级比较用 as tiny as。
tiny 意为“微小”，笔记簿上那半行字要的是“微小的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something tiny。
tiny 意为“微小”，邻教室来的那位学童认为这套计划“相当微小”，quite 修饰原级 tiny。
tiny 意为“微小”，1980 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要微小”，故用比较级 tinier than。
tiny 意为“微小”，母亲 1982 年说的是“整个教室里最微小的那一桩”，故用最高级 the tiniest house by the road。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1970 年，先生在笔记簿里记下了一件极小的种子。（a tiny seed in the packet）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更极小。（tinier than …）
母亲觉得它太极小，谁也用不上。（too tiny to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩微小的房子。（a tiny house by the road）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩路边小小的房子一样微小。（as tiny as …）
到了 1977 年，笔记簿上只剩半行字：要的是一件微小的东西。（something tiny）
answers: In 1970 the teacher wrote of a tiny seed in the packet in the notebook.
Everybody said it was tinier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too tiny to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a tiny house by the road.
He said nobody would call it as tiny as the house by the road they had once had.
By 1977 the notebook asked for nothing but something tiny.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 tiny 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1970 the teacher wrote of a tiny seed in the packet in the notebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the tiniest seed in the packet in the classroom, or so the notebook says.
My mother thought it too tiny to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a tiny house by the road, and nobody argued with him.
The pupil from the next classroom called the plan quite tiny, and everybody laughed.
The tiny ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
